reject_reason: other: invalid evidence: the published CPU-vs-GPU encoder and kernel numbers cannot have been produced by the repository's code. There is no encoder, the reproduction flags in docs/benchmarks.md do not exist in the test binary, the only CPU-vs-SYCL timing test is disabled and times the CPU function twice, and the repo's own TEST_REPORT.md says no GPU was ever tested.
tier_reason: docs/benchmarks.md does contain the fps and kernel tables quoted in the record. Its only baseline is an unnamed 'CPU Baseline' (no AVM version, encoder settings or CPU named for that column). No code in the repo can produce those tables. tests/sycl_perf_test.cpp's main() only calls InitGoogleTest/RUN_ALL_TESTS, so the documented '--benchmark --iterations=1000 --warmup=100' and '--csv=results.csv' flags do not exist. Its CPU-vs-SYCL test, DISABLED_TransformPerformance, is disabled, and its 'SYCL' loop calls av2_fwd_txfm2d_c on the CPU ('placeholder - uses CPU for now', 'TODO: Replace with actual SYCL kernel'). The repo has no SAD, loop-filter or intra CPU-vs-GPU benchmark, and no encoder at all.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Claimed in docs/benchmarks.md: Intel DPC++ 2024.0, GCC 11.4, CUDA 12.2, CMake 3.28, Release build. The repo's only actual test log (docs/TEST_REPORT.md, 2026-03-18) used Intel DPC++ 2025.3 on the OpenCL CPU backend.
corrections.hardware: Claimed: i9-13900K + RTX 4090, i7-12700K + RTX 3080, i7-12700K + Arc A770, Ryzen 9 7950X + RX 7900 XTX. The only measured run in the repo (docs/TEST_REPORT.md) is an Intel Xeon Gold 6530 via the OpenCL CPU backend, and that report states 'GPU backend not tested'.
corrections.caveats: Evidence judged invalid. (1) The repo holds SYCL kernels (src/sycl_txfm, sycl_me, sycl_lpf, sycl_intra), a context wrapper and src/av2/common/enums.h, but no AV2/AVM encoder, so the 'Full Encoding Pipeline' fps table cannot come from this code. tests/CMakeLists.txt links avm_encoder/avm_decoder targets that are not in the repo. (2) docs/benchmarks.md tells readers to run './tests/sycl_perf_test --benchmark --iterations=1000 --warmup=100 --csv=results.csv'. tests/sycl_perf_test.cpp has no such options (plain gtest main). Its only CPU-vs-SYCL test is DISABLED_TransformPerformance, whose 'SYCL' timing loop calls the same CPU function av2_fwd_txfm2d_c ('placeholder - uses CPU for now'). tests/sycl_optimized_perf_test.cpp compares two SYCL variants with each other, not against the CPU, and the root CMakeLists.txt does not build it. Nothing benchmarks SAD, loop filter or intra prediction against a CPU path. (3) The repo's own docs/TEST_REPORT.md (2026-03-18) ran 4 smoke tests on a Xeon Gold 6530 through the OpenCL CPU backend: DCT 8x8 averaged 50.14 us, and a 1024-element vector add took 287.5 ms. It states 'GPU backend not tested' because an RTX 5090 was not reachable via SYCL. Yet the README says the speedup was 'verified on Intel Core i9-13900K + NVIDIA RTX 4090', and benchmarks.md ('Last updated: March 2026') lists RTX 4090/3080/Arc A770/RX 7900 XTX results. (4) Internal contradictions: the README's GPU table gives the RX 7900 XTX power efficiency 1.2x, benchmarks.md gives 0.9x, and the README's platform table marks AMD HIP support as in progress while benchmarks.md reports 88 fps at 1080p30 on that card. (5) The LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause-Clear with 'Copyright (c) 2026, Alliance for Open Media'. That license is FSF-free but not OSI-approved and grants no patent rights. The citation block's Zenodo DOI could not be checked (zenodo blocked).

notes: Reject for invalid evidence, as the search agent suspected: the tables look fabricated or are at least unsupported by any code or log in the repo, and the repo's only real test log contradicts them. tier_reason: First-party numbers. The harness, scripts/bench-encoders.sh, is public and fixes level 5, single thread and a deterministic generated input, and CPU models (i7-1260P, Cortex-A76) are stated. The Go toolchain version, ffmpeg/flac/sox versions and builds, and OS are not stated, and each encoder is timed once, so it is not A. The 16/24/32-bit snapshot (about 19 ms vs about 71 ms) has no harness in the repo and no stated machine.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: go-flac built with plain 'go build' (default flags; Go toolchain version not stated, go.mod declares go 1.27). Baselines run as 'ffmpeg -threads 1 -c:a flac -compression_level 5', 'flac -5 -f -s', 'sox -C 5'; their versions and builds are not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party claim with a public harness (scripts/bench-encoders.sh). That harness supports only the throughput claim, and modestly: on the harness table go-flac is 1.15x (amd64) and 1.06x (arm64) faster than ffmpeg's flac encoder (derived from page data). libFLAC is about 1.5x faster than go-flac. Each encoder is timed once with GNU time, so the wall time includes process start-up and WAV parsing, and the arm64 margin is within run-to-run noise. All encoders run level 5, single-threaded, on the same file, so they do comparable work. The default input is a synthetic 440 Hz sine plus white-noise mono mix (ratio about 0.85), not music. The README contradicts itself on compression ratio. 'Audio quality' says go-flac 'encodes faster and slightly smaller than ffmpeg's FLAC'. The benchmark section says it 'matches libFLAC's compression ratio exactly and beats ffmpeg on both throughput and ratio on each architecture'. Yet the README's own harness table lists go-flac 0.8523 vs ffmpeg 0.8519 (and SoX 0.8519), so ffmpeg's output is smaller and the ratio claim is contradicted by the only harnessed data. 'Slightly smaller' rests only on the 16-bit row of the 2026-09-05 snapshot (0.45 vs 0.46; 24-bit equal at 0.64; 32-bit 0.51 vs 0.48 where ffmpeg truncates to 24-bit). That snapshot has no script in the repo, no stated machine, and the README calls it 'a small directional sample'; a corpus-based gate is still open as issue #45. Young repo (commits from July 2026).

notes: Confirmed at C. Of the two README statements, only the throughput claim is supported by a harness; the ratio-win claim is contradicted by the README's own table. Language Go is correct (already set in the record). Metadata checked: MIT, 2 stars, 1 fork, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-08, active.

tier_reason: The 0.5.4 release notes give first-party single-thread timings and sizes for HALAC -plus/-normal against FLAC 1.5.0 -8/-5 and name the CPU ('AMD Ryzen 9 9600X'). There is no benchmark script, OS, compiler, FLAC build or timing method, the test albums are not distributed, and the measured 0.5.4 encoder is a closed Windows binary. That is tier C.

corrections.baseline: FLAC 1.5.0 (flac CLI) at -8 and -5. The 0.5.4 notes also list WavPack 5.9.0 -h and HALAC 0.5.1. Monkey's Audio, WavPack and OptimFROG (versions not stated) appear only in the 0.4.8 notes for the 32-bit float set.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Release 0.5.4 notes, 'AMD Ryzen 9 9600X, Single Thread', six BipTunia albums, 5,883,941,384 bytes of 24-bit/44.1 kHz stereo WAV. HALAC 0.5.4 -plus: 4,232,751,891 bytes, 11.578 s encode, 13.201 s decode. FLAC 1.5.0 -8: 4,243,522,638 bytes, 50.802 s, 14.357 s. That is about 4.4x faster encode and 1.09x faster decode with 0.25% smaller output (derived from page data). HALAC 0.5.4 -normal: 4,268,470,589 bytes, 7.200 s, 9.353 s. FLAC 1.5.0 -5: 4,265,600,750 bytes, 15.857 s, 13.451 s. That is about 2.2x faster encode and 1.44x faster decode with 0.07% larger output (derived from page data). WavPack 5.9.0 -h: 4,263,185,834 bytes, 64.855 s, 49.367 s. Release 0.4.8 notes, 29 tracks of 32-bit float stereo, 2,089,718,160 bytes, 'HALAC AVX2 Single thread', no FLAC row. HALAC normal 1,381,439,835 bytes, 3.050 s / 4.290 s, versus WavPack fast 1,392,225,168 bytes, 20.675 s / 13.914 s, and OptimFROG fast 1,346,477,460 bytes, 39.310 s / 32.179 s.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated. 0.5.4 ships closed Windows executables built for AVX, AVX2 and AVX512, and the notes do not say which was timed; the 0.4.8 notes say 'HALAC AVX2 Single thread'. FLAC 1.5.0 build and options beyond -8/-5 are not stated.
corrections.hardware: 'AMD Ryzen 9 9600X' as written in the 0.5.4 notes (AMD sells the 9600X as a Ryzen 5), single thread. OS not stated; the release assets are Windows .exe files.
corrections.caveats: First-party release-note numbers with no benchmark script, compiler, OS or timing method, and the test albums are not distributed, so tier C. The measured code is not public. The repository source is only v0.1.9 (halac_encode/decode_v.0.1.9 plus FSE), last changed 2025-11-17. Its encoder prints 'Only 16 bit, 2 channels .wav types are supported for input!', reads 2-byte samples, and its main() walks a hard-coded Windows test directory, so it cannot even encode the 24-bit benchmark set. The release 'Source code' archives for 0.4.8 and 0.5.4 are that same 2025-11-17 snapshot, and the 0.5.4 encoder exists only as HALAC_ENCODE_0.5.4_AVX/AVX2/AVX512.exe (2026-04-10). The comparison names the machine and the settings (single thread; HALAC -plus vs FLAC -8 and -normal vs FLAC -5, levels paired by similar output size). It does not say whether FLAC's default whole-stream MD5 and per-frame CRCs were left on. The public v0.1.9 encoder computes no MD5 or CRC, so if 0.5.4 also skips them, the two encoders do different integrity work. The headline 4.4x is against FLAC's slowest standard preset; against -5 it is 2.2x encode, and the decode gap is small (1.09x to 1.44x). Releases continue to 0.6.6 (dated 26 Sep, year not shown). Independent threads on hydrogenaudio and encode.su exist but are blocked from this environment. FLAC is not in this category's baseline list.

notes: Confirmed at C with has_code set to false: the benchmarked 0.5.4 build is binary-only, and the repo's v0.1.9 source is a 16-bit-only early version that cannot reproduce the 24-bit test. usability left as 'mixed' (MIT v0.1.9 source copyable, measured version closed). The orchestrator may prefer 'reference'. Metadata checked: MIT, 48 stars, 4 forks, not a fork, last commit 2025-11-17 (active), latest release 0.6.6.
